content.text: CAPACITY & COMPETENCY
Competency:
legal (court)        -
Capacity:
clinical -functional assessment by provider familiar w pt case
Capacity Eval Components:
Communication:
express tx choice, explain rational for chg decisions
Understanding:
recall convos about tx, process outcomes
Appreciation:
identify illness, tx options, likely outcomes that will affect them
Rationalization & Reasoning:
weight risk & benefits, come to conclusions keeping w their goals
COMMUNITY & SYSTEMS
Resource Variation:            -     County                        -     Government funding: state & federal             -    Dx
Income              -    Insurance                    -     Timing of services needed
Key Resource:
Social workers → d/c planning, community resources, referrals
Medicare Basics
Eligibility:       -
Age ±65             -    ALS, ESRD                -     SSDI: ±24M on disability
Part A:   -
Hsp       -    Skilled nursing      -    Hospice      -    Home health      -    Nursing home
Part B:   -
Medical services                     -     Preventive care
Not covered (unless Advantage Plan):
-   Long-term care   -  Dental/dentures     -   Eye exams    -  Cosmetic surgery    -  Routine physicals   -   Hearing aids
Coverage Rules:                                                                               **No payment if readmitted w/in 30 days (if same Dx)**
3-day hsp stay → skilled nursing facility coverage        -     Covers 120 days in extended care facility
COMMUNITY PROGRAMS
Center for Senior Independence: seniors stay in home & communities as long as possible
Alt to assisted living         -    Day program (1–5 days/wk)      -    Provides meals, tx, meds, transport
Meals on Wheels:    -    Home-delivered meals (usually lunch & dinner)        -    ↑demand:  Wait time: ~2 weeks–1 M
ELDER ABUSE
Mandatory Reporters (MI): Physicians         -   Home health    -     Mental health providers      -    Law enforcement
RF:Limited resources: ex covid-19, Caregiver stress/substance use
Signs           Injuries: cuts, bruises, sprains               -    Easily upset, emotional w/drawal          -    Sudden behavioral chg
Meds misuse: overdose or w/held       -    Restricted visitation by caregivers          -    Broken glasses
Financial exploitation: sudden transfers, sudden will chgs, sudden banking chgs, new names
Senior ER:  Geriatric-trained staff            -   Higher staffing ratio       -   Case mgnt               -    Private rooms
Safer environment: lighting, floors, mattresses               -    Sensory aids readily available
M’s of gerniatric care                                                                                                                assoc team:
Mind
-    depression, anxiety, impairment                                                   -    neurology, psychology, psychiatry
Meds:
-    polypharmacy, optimal prescribing, adverse effects                -    doctor of pharmacy
Multicomplexity:
mng multi-morbid,                                                                 -    all healthcare professionals
geriatric syndrome & biopsychosocial complexity
Mobility:
gait, function, mobility aids, exercise, frailty                                   -    PT/OT, nutrition, orthopedic, neurology
Matters Most;:
align care w pt's goals of care, advance care planning        -    social work, nurse, pharmacist, palliative
FOLEY/URINARY CATH
Straight cath:
short-term use     -
Foley cath:
long-term/indwelling
INDICATIONS FOR CATH PLACEMENT
Bladder drainage                                  -    Control bleed (apply P)                 -    Bladder irrigation
Deliver antineoplastic agents            -    Measure PVR                                   -    Pre-op sterile field
Obstructed bladder                             -    Obtain sterile urine sample          -    Monitor I/O’s
Neurogenic bladder                            -    Stabilize skin graft post-urethral surgery
***convenience/lack of proper nursing care for Incontinence = never indication to place***
Straight cath Indications:
Obtain sterile urine sample      -    Acute decompression of bladder: acute obstruction or processes
Intermittent cath                        -    Deliver topical bladder meds                  -     Assess PVR: if ⍉POCUS
Self-cath (Scheduled) -indication:  Spinal cord injury     -    Neurogenic bladder                 **Medicare: 300 single-use/M, 6/day
Suprapubic cath Indications: Long-term use              -   Urethral transection                    -    Obstruction
CONTRAINDICATIONS OF CATH
Allergy: cath materials      -  Blood @urethral meatus: pelvic trauma or saddle injuries  - sus urethral transection
Sx/S Urethral Transection: Blood @meatus     -    High-riding prostate    -     Perineal/scrotal hematoma      -    Pelvic frx
POST-VOID RESIDUAL (PVR)                                                             **exact PVR = w cath, est PVR w US **
measure PVR: L x W x D x 0.52
Norm: < 100mL                                -     acceptable: 200mL        -    inadequate voiding: +200mL
indicating retention: 300mL          -     retention: 400mL
Causes of Retention:    -   Obstruction      -    Neurogenic bladder      -    Spinal cord injury
TYPES OF CATHS:
Robinson cath
: 1-way -> self-cath   - red rubber
Robinson 2-Way:
Silicone (latex allergy)   - norm
Coude:
Curved tip   - maneuver around lrg prostate or obstruction
Robinson Three-way Foley:
1. Balloon inflation    2. Irrigation    3.  Urine drainage
SIZING: on inflation port                                                                                                                             3 Fr = 1 mm diameter
Pediatrics: 4–12 Fr      -    Adult female: ~14 Fr     -    Adult male: 16–18 Fr    -    Urologic bleeding: 20–30 Fr
PROCEDURE EQUIPMENT:                                                                            (cleaning genitalia)
Sterile: gloves/drapes, cotton ball, forceps, lub/anesthetic gel, syringe w sterile H2O, Antiseptic: betadine ×3
Cath, Leg strap/tape/leg bag       -    Urine collection bag           -    Towel
PEARLS: Use sterile technique       -    Use sm cath poss     -    Secure cath properly    -    Use closed drainage system
B4 Emptying Bag: Record output for I/O tracking
Positioning Rule: Keep bag
below pt level
→ ↓reflux & ↓UTIs
C
OMPLICATIONS:    Urethral dilation          -    pt-induced trauma             -    Improper securing/taping     -    Tech difficulty
cath looping/double back        -    False passage (fistula)       -     Intravaginal placement         -    Urethral trauma
CATH-ASSOC UTI (CAUTI): Eti:
MC:
E. coli        -Enterococcus, Staphylococcus, Pseudomonas, Candida, Proteus (chronic caths)
RF: ↑duration → ↑risk
Prevention:    Avoid unnecessary cath use: consider alt                         -    Remove as early as poss, use US when poss
Maintain sterile tech       -   re-eval if pt needs cath        -    Use sm cath        -    Closed drainage system
